origin.text: TODAY credits UK-based account Eat with GG with sparking the recent wave, noting such combos have circulated for years. A video by Australian creator Jaz Hand Made and friends then went viral, which Know Your Meme says happened in late September 2026 (we saw this only in a search summary).

productDemand.text: No purchase evidence found. Interest is curiosity and entertainment. The party-game angle is our inference based on the group format of the videos.

trajectory.text: Recent and spreading across outlets, but evidence is thin: one big video (reported nearly 2M TikTok views) and a handful of copycats. Too early to say whether it grows or fades in a few weeks.

what: Creators and groups of friends try simple two-ingredient combos that people say taste like something else, filming their reactions. Commonly cited pairs are cucumber with sugar (watermelon), tomato with chips (pizza) or sugar (strawberry), banana with avocado (ice cream) and lemon with cinnamon (cola). It works as a group activity, which is what makes a party format possible.

window.estimate: 4-8 weeks of relevance as a viral reference; the party-game use stays seasonal
invalidators: No new creator videos or articles after mid-October
A major party-supply brand releases a similar game
window.reasoning: Food-video curiosities usually fade within weeks, but the product works as a general party game through the November-December hosting season even after the trend fades.
window.seasonality: Halloween through New Year party season
